content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Jennifer Martin (E033), requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory has two notes:
- Note 1: role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation for Payroll: write. Comment: full-time Analyst, requested admin but Payroll owned by Payroll Specialist role, admin not permitted, max write.
- Note 2: role Analyst, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation for Payroll: read. Comment: security record shows contractor with basic training (note conflicts; security DB is authoritative). Contractors never get admin; with basic training max read.

So there's a conflict between notes. Note 2 says security DB is authoritative and shows contractor with basic training. The security agent's note takes precedence? The comment says "note conflicts; security DB is authoritative."

According to the policy:
- full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
- contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

If contractor with basic training: max read. Requested admin exceeds read, so grant read.

Note 2's comment says the security record is authoritative. So employment type is contractor, basic training. Max = read. Requested admin > read, grant read.

The recommendation from security agent is read. That seems to be the decisive one.

So decision: read.

Evidence: Security note (authoritative) says E033 is contractor with basic training; contractors never get admin, max read; requested admin exceeds read, so grant read.
